findings.how_to_check: Audit a sample of profiles where has_dmonth==1 in FamilySearch Family Tree to inspect the change log for fullname. Check what fraction had their primary name established by attaching the 1940 census index vs an independent vital record.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not describe the death-month subgroup as establishing independence from the census index or mitigating common-source bias. Frame it strictly as a descriptive subgroup analysis (e.g., profiles with post-1940 vital records attached), or validate name provenance directly using external, hand-verified ground truth.
findings.title: Conditioning on a death month does not establish that profile names are independent of the attached census index
findings.what_the_code_does: The code constructs has_dmonth using a regex check on deathdate (lines 148-155) and scores agreement on this subgroup (lines 278-286), claiming in comments that 'a profile with a death month was built from sources beyond the census, and its name is less likely to be a copy of the attached census index'. In fact, the code only observes that an external death fact was attached to the profile; it does not observe or condition on the provenance of fullname, which is often populated directly from FamilySearch's 1940 census index when the record is attached.
findings.why_it_matters: FamilySearch profiles routinely combine a name initially populated from FamilySearch's 1940 census index with later-attached vital records (e.g., SSDI). Restricting to profiles with a death month does not remove FamilySearch's mechanical advantage or validate claims of transcription accuracy. Presenting this subgroup as an independence robustness check risks rejection by referees familiar with FamilySearch linkage dynamics.

findings.how_to_check: Search for profile_names in replication/ using `git grep -n "profile_names" replication/`. Run `git diff MATCHING/results/profile_names.md` to confirm the Markdown exhibit has not been regenerated with the death-month blocks.
findings.suggested_fix: Integrate profile_names_build.do and profile_names_score.do into the replication pipeline (or document a dedicated appendix replication runner) and run the script to commit the updated MATCHING/results/profile_names.md containing the new score blocks.
findings.title: The modified profile scoring script is omitted from the replication master and results are not updated
findings.what_the_code_does: The uncommitted changes add six new scoreblock executions for death-month subgroups to MATCHING/profile_names_score.do (lines 280-285). However, neither profile_names_build.do nor profile_names_score.do is invoked anywhere in replication/run_machineA.do (lines 92-132), and the output file MATCHING/results/profile_names.md has not been regenerated or committed with the new blocks (it still ends after Rule (3)).
findings.why_it_matters: An independent replicator running the documented replication suite (run_machineA.do) will not execute this analysis or reproduce these tables. Furthermore, the repository's tracked output file profile_names.md is out of sync with the scoring code, leaving the reported results stale.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect lines 128-133 of MATCHING/profile_names_score.do: `local t_ref = clock(\`"c(filedate)"\', "DMYhm")` and `local t_pn = clock(\`"pn_date"\', "DMYhm")`. Notice that no check on script hash or normalization version is performed.
findings.suggested_fix: Include a code version or checksum token in the cache metadata (or embed a version string in the cache filename), and invalidate the cache if the token does not match the current script version.
findings.title: Split-name cache checks file modification time but ignores changes to normalization and parsing code
findings.what_the_code_does: Lines 125-136 reuse cached refs_*.dta files whenever t_ref > t_pn (i.e. the cache file header date is newer than profile_names.dta). The cache validity check does not verify the version, checksum, or code of pnorm, xsplit, or extrname. Instead, a comment at lines 114-115 instructs the user to manually delete refs_*.dta whenever normalization changes.
findings.why_it_matters: If a researcher modifies name normalization rules in pnorm (e.g., adding/modifying suffixes, punctuation, or nickname handling), subsequent runs will silently reuse stale split names from disk without throwing an error or warning, causing silent divergence between code and results.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied; claims-vs-code review was limited to claims, comments, and exhibit headers in code and results rather than paper text.

Data files in external directories (D:\Dropbox\..., F:\..., E:\...) were not accessible, and the Stata pipeline could not be executed; runtime data distribution and exact execution times could not be verified.
Stata executable was not present in the environment; all Stata language semantics and macro expansions were verified via static source code tracing.
Review scope was targeted to uncommitted changes in the working tree and associated replication master scripts rather than a full codebase re-audit.
summary: The working-tree change introduces a death-month subgroup analysis to test whether profile-name agreement holds among profiles built from non-census sources, alongside a performance cache for split names. However, the presence of an attached death date does not establish that the profile's name was sourced independently of FamilySearch's census index, leaving the core endogeneity unaddressed. In addition, the new analysis is absent from the replication pipeline and tracked exhibits, and the caching mechanism relies on manual deletion rather than code versioning.
